causes.text: On April 2 2023, members of the OPEC+ alliance including Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, Kuwait, Oman and Algeria announced voluntary production cuts totalling 1.15 million barrels per day to support market stability.

source_info.title: OPEC+ announces surprise oil output cuts

effects.text: In May 2023 BP reduced its share-buyback programme from $2.75 billion to $1.75 billion, prompting its largest daily share price drop in more than three years.

source_info.title: BP's profit hits $5 billion but shares slip on slowing buybacks

causal_reasoning_chain.description: OPEC+ members unexpectedly agreed to voluntarily cut more than a million barrels of oil per day, signalling tighter supply and potentially higher prices.
The production cuts lifted crude prices and heightened investor expectations that oil majors would return more cash to shareholders, BP's profit hits $5 billion
But BP subsequently announced a smaller share-buyback programme than anticipated.
The divergence from heightened expectations led investors to sell, causing BP's share price to drop 8% despite the supportive oil-price environment.

rationale: The surprise OPEC+ cuts raised oil prices and primed investors for generous shareholder returns. BP's decision to slow its buybacks disappointed those expectations, resulting in a notable share price decline.
counterfactual_analysis: If OPEC+ had not tightened supply, crude prices would have remained subdued and investor expectations for buybacks lower, so BP's announcement might not have triggered such a steep drop.

adversarial_confounders.text: Variations in refining margins and company-specific operational issues
adversarial_confounders.impact: Could influence both cause and effect by altering market perceptions.
